stories.summary: If the Aboriginal woman had been checked at regular intervals as required, her ‘excess consumption of water’ would have been prevented, inquest finds • Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The death of an Aboriginal woman who collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water in a New South Wales prison cell was preventable and the result of systemic failures, a coroner has found. stories.title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade
stories.summary: Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment. Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan , drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers. Continue reading...

stories.title: Tulip Siddiq says she is considering legal action against former Bangladesh leader

The MP for Hampstead and Highgate, whose aunt Sheikh Hasina was put on trial in absentia over crimes against humanity during her 15 years as prime minister of Bangladesh, was accused of benefiting from the former regime by the authorities in the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka. stories.title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking
stories.summary: HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland. Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898. Continue reading...

stories.title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia
stories.summary: Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant. A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird, with populations that visit Britain spending summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter. Continue reading...

stories.title: Weight-loss drugs used in nearly one in 10 homes in Great Britain, study finds
stories.summary: About 2.6m adults are taking the drugs, fuelled by the regulator’s approval of the pill versions and a rise in male users At least one person is taking weight-loss drugs in 8.5% of households in Great Britain, according to research, meaning there are more homes with GLP-1 users than those containing vegetarians and pescatarians combined. About 2.6 million adults were using weight-loss medication in August, a rise of about 700,000 people since February, according to a survey by Worldpanel by Numerator . Continue reading...

stories.title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns
stories.summary: Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog. The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.
